post.title: Travel scam losses more than doubled in one year
post.ig:
Travel scams cost Americans $274 million in 2024, per FTC reports.
FTC Consumer Sentinel losses for travel, vacation and timeshare scams: $104M in 2022, $122M in 2023, $274M in 2024. Reports rose only about 6% (55,063 to 58,347).
The median reported loss in 2024 was $922, nearly double the $497 median for all fraud.
The BBB says fake agencies push big package discounts, take payment upfront and vanish. The FTC says demands for wire, gift card or crypto payment are a scam sign; credit cards give the most protection, and the Fair Credit Billing Act lets you dispute an undelivered purchase in writing within 60 days of the statement.
Sources: FTC Consumer Sentinel Data Books 2022-2024, FTC consumer guidance, BBB.
News and education, not financial advice.
